title: Shangri-La International Hotel v. Developers Group
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the conflict between prior use and registration of trademarks. The Court held that in the Philippines, the trademark system follows the first-to-file rule under the IP Code, but prior use may still confer rights in certain circumstances.
doctrine: Under the Intellectual Property Code, the Philippines adopted the first-to-file system for trademark registration. However, a prior user in good faith may continue to use the mark within the area of actual use. Registration creates a prima facie presumption of ownership, but this may be rebutted by evidence of prior use.
fullText:
CARPIO MORALES, J.:

This case involves a trademark dispute between two entities claiming the right to use the 'Shangri-La' mark for hotel and resort services.

The Intellectual Property Code, Republic Act No. 8293, adopted the first-to-file system for the registration of trademarks. Under this system, the first person to file an application for registration of a trademark shall have the right to register the same.

However, the first-to-file rule does not completely disregard prior use. Section 138 of the IP Code provides that a certificate of registration is prima facie evidence of the validity of the registration, the registrant's ownership of the mark, and the registrant's exclusive right to use the same. This presumption, however, may be rebutted.
